Motivation
Share groups redeliver a released record immediately, so a transient failure can use up all of a record's delivery attempts immediately. This KIP lets a share group wait before redelivering such a record, with an optional exponential backoff that grows with each attempt.
With share groups (KIP-932), a consumer that cannot process a record acknowledges it withAcknowledgeType.RELEASE. The record is then available for another delivery attempt straight away. The same happens when the record's acquisition lock times out, or when the consumer holding it disconnects.
Immediate redelivery suits failures that are unlikely to recur, such as a consumer crash. It works badly for failures that last seconds or minutes, example - a downstream service is unavailable or throttling, a database fails over etc. The record fails again at once, reaches the delivery count limit (group.share.delivery.count.limit, default 5) and is archived and written to the dead-letter queue (KIP-1191, if configured), although its processing could have succeeded a little later.
Public Interfaces
This KIP adds three group configurations, one broker configuration and one share-partition metric. It changes no RPCs, no records in__share_group_statetopic and no client APIs.
Group configuration
These are set per share group withkafka-configs.shorAdmin.incrementalAlterConfigson theGROUPresource. As with the existing share group configurations, a value outside the broker's minimum and maximum is rejected when it is set.
